title: Machine-learning regression assists dual-mode ochratoxin A sensing
summary: A study led by COMSATS University reports a cerium–cobalt metal-organic-framework sensor for ochratoxin A, combining fluorescence and electrochemical measurements with machine-learning regression of fluorescence data for quantitative analysis. The publisher abstract reports real-sample recoveries of101.31–102.05% for fluorescence and103.05–105.50% for electrochemistry, checked against HPLC. This is a bounded experimental analytical result; the reviewed abstract does not name the regression algorithms or establish broad field deployment. Full subscription methods were not assessed in this review.
ai_technology: Supervised machine-learning regression of fluorescence measurements (algorithms not named in reviewed abstract)
organization: COMSATS University Islamabad; University of the Punjab; Islamic University of Madinah; King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals; Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: Initial dual-mode sensor experiments and real-sample recovery analysis, with HPLC comparison; the source says regression models analyze fluorescence data quantitatively.
evidence.unknown: Named regression algorithms, training/test partitions and their incremental contribution were not stated in the reviewed abstract; subscription full methods were not assessed. Broad food-matrix generalization and field use are not established.
evidence.ai_role: Learned regression maps fluorescence measurements to quantitative analyte predictions, supporting the reported sensor analysis; generative writing/code assistance acknowledged elsewhere is a separate role.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher abstract, affiliations, publication metadata and visible AI-assistance statement; subscription full methods not assessed
